'''Grace Goldsmith Wahba''' (born August 3, 1934) is an American statistician and retired I. J. Schoenberg-Hilldale Professor of [[Statistics]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref name="Breaking ground with Grace">{{Cite web|url=https://news.wisc.edu/breaking-ground-with-grace/|title=Breaking ground with Grace|website=news.wisc.edu|language=en-US|access-date=2018-11-16}}</ref> She is a pioneer in methods for [[smoothing]] [[noisy data]]. Best known for the development of generalized [[cross-validation (statistics)|cross-validation]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Craven|first1=Peter|last2=Wahba|first2=Grace|date=1978-12-01|title=Smoothing noisy data with spline functions|journal=Numerische Mathematik|language=en|volume=31|issue=4|pages=377–403|doi=10.1007/BF01404567|s2cid=14094416|issn=0945-3245}}</ref> and "[[Wahba's problem]]",<ref name="Breaking ground with Grace"/> she has developed methods with applications in [[Demography|demographic studies]], [[machine learning]], [[DNA microarrays]], [[risk modeling]], [[medical imaging]], and [[Numerical weather prediction|climate prediction]].

==Biography==
Wahba had an interest in science from an early age, when she was in junior high she was given a chemistry set.<ref name=":0" /> At this time she was also interested in becoming an engineer.<ref name=":0" />

Wahba studied at Cornell University for her undergraduate degree; in 1952, Cornell and [[Brown University]] were the only Ivy League universities that admitted women.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> When she was there women were severely restricted in their privileges, for example she was required to live in a dorm and had a curfew.<ref name=":0" /> She received her bachelor's degree from [[Cornell University]] in 1956 and a master's degree from the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in 1962.<ref name="Breaking ground with Grace"/> She worked in industry for several years before receiving her doctorate from Stanford University in 1966 and settling in [[Madison, Wisconsin|Madison]] in 1967.

She is the author of ''Spline Models for Observational Data''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Spline Models for Observational Data|last=Wahba|first=G.|date=1990-01-01|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|isbn=9780898712445|series=CBMS-NSF Regional Conference Series in Applied Mathematics|doi=10.1137/1.9781611970128|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/splinemodelsforo0000wahb}}</ref> She retired in August 2018 from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://statistics.stanford.edu/people/grace-goldsmith-wahba|title=Grace Goldsmith Wahba {{!}} Department of Statistics|website=statistics.stanford.edu|access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
[[File:Grace Wahba 2010.jpg|thumb|left|upright| Wahba in 2010 |alt=]]

Wahba was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1997<ref>{{cite web|title=Grace Wahba|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/grace-wahba|website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref> and to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web|title=National Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/grace-wahba-a8qf3w/|website=|access-date=22 February 2016}}</ref> She is also a fellow of several academic societies including the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Statistical Association]], and the  [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref name="wahba">{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.wisc.edu/~wahba/hons.txt|website=|access-date=22 February 2016|title=Grace Wahba: Honors}}</ref>

Over the years she has received a selection of notable awards in the statistics community:

* [[International Prize in Statistics]], 2025<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statprize.org/2025-International-Prize-in-Statistics-Awarded-to-Grace-Wahba.cfm|title=Grace Wahba Honored with International Prize for Work on Smoothing Splines|publisher=International Prize in Statistics|last=Va|first=Alexandria|date=April 14, 2025|access-date=April 29, 2025}}</ref>
* [[R. A. Fisher Lectureship]], [[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies|COPSS]], August 2014<ref name="ims">{{cite web|title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|url=http://www.imstat.org/awards/copss_recipients.htm|website=|access-date=22 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312212858/http://imstat.org/awards/copss_recipients.htm|archive-date=12 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[Gottfried E. Noether]] Senior Researcher Award, Joint Statistics Meetings, August 2009
* Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies Elizabeth Scott Award, 1996<ref name="ims" />
* First [[Parzen Prize|Emanuel and Carol Parzen Prize for Statistical Innovation]], 1994

She received honorary [[Doctor of Science]] degrees from the University of Chicago in 2007 and The Ohio State University in 2022.

The Institute of Mathematical Statistics announced the IMS Grace Wahba Award and Lecture in 2021.<ref name="ims-grace-wahba-award-and-lecture">{{Cite web|url=https://stat.wisc.edu/2021/05/27/ims-grace-wahba-award-and-lecture//|title=ims-grace-wahba-award-and-lecture|date=27 May 2021 |access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref>
